title: "RFK Jr. has lied to the Senate": Lawmakers call for criminal probe, ouster
gist: Newly released documents show Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. wrote to Samoa's prime minister in 2019 proposing his group investigate the country's MMR vaccine supply, directly contradicting his sworn 2025 Senate confirmation testimony that his Samoa trip had 'nothing to do with vaccines,' prompting senators to call for his resignation, firing, or a criminal DOJ probe.

insights.claim: During his January 2025 confirmation hearings, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. told Sen. Ron Wyden and Sen. Ed Markey that his 2019 trip to Samoa had nothing to do with vaccines, claiming he went to introduce a medical informatics system to digitalize health records.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Establishes the specific sworn claim that newly released documents are alleged to contradict, which is the basis for the criminal-referral calls.
insights.quote: I went there, [it had] nothing to do with vaccines. I went there to introduce a medical informatics system that would digitalize records in Samoa and make health delivery much more efficient.
insights.locator: paragraph on Kennedy's exchange with Wyden

insights.claim: A January 2019 letter from Kennedy to Samoa's prime minister, jointly released by the Associated Press and The Guardian, used the words 'vaccine' or 'vaccination' eight times and proposed that Kennedy and his Children's Health Defense team investigate the country's MMR vaccine supply, directly contradicting his sworn claim that the trip had nothing to do with vaccines.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: This is the documentary evidence senators are citing as proof of perjury before Congress, the trigger for the criminal-investigation request.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'One of the documents is a letter Kennedy sent'

insights.claim: Sen. Ron Wyden called the newly released documents proof that Kennedy lied on the record during his confirmation hearing, characterized this as a crime, and called for a Department of Justice criminal investigation.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: A sitting senator explicitly requesting a DOJ criminal referral against a cabinet secretary is a significant escalation with potential legal and political consequences beyond calls for resignation.
insights.quote: RFK’s platform is built on lies and grifts that leave a trail of dead children in their wake. There are consequences for lying to Congress.
insights.locator: quote from Ron Wyden to The Guardian

insights.claim: Sen. Ed Markey characterized the contradiction as part of a pattern, not an isolated slip, saying Kennedy has lied to the Senate and the American people to advance his anti-vaccine agenda.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Framing this as a pattern rather than a one-off increases the political durability of calls for Kennedy's removal.
insights.quote: This is a pattern, not a slip,

insights.claim: Kennedy's 2019 letter falsely suggested that two infant deaths in Samoa were caused by a bad lot of MMR vaccines from the manufacturer, when officials had determined the deaths were caused by two nurses mixing the vaccine with a lethal dose of muscle relaxant; the nurses were convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to five years in prison in August 2019.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Establishes that the factual premise Kennedy used to justify his Samoa intervention was false, since the deaths were a documented medical-error and criminal case, not a vaccine-safety failure.

insights.claim: Children's Health Defense and other anti-vaccine activists spent months publicizing the infant deaths on Facebook as evidence against MMR vaccine safety, without ever updating those posts once the nurses' fatal dosing error was established.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Shows a specific, sustained misinformation campaign that was not corrected even after the true cause of death was publicly known, a factor cited in fueling the subsequent outbreak.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'In the meantime, CHD and other anti-vaccine activists pounced'

insights.claim: Samoa's vaccination rate fell to as low as 31 percent amid vaccine hesitancy stoked by anti-vaccine activism, and the country's October 2019 measles outbreak killed 83 people, mostly children under age 5; a WHO official directly tied the outbreak to an anti-vaccine group's social media fearmongering.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Quantifies the real-world death toll linked by a WHO official to the anti-vaccine campaign Kennedy's group waged in Samoa in the months before the outbreak.
insights.quote: now being measured in the lives of children who have died in the course of this outbreak
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'Samoa's deadly measles outbreak began in October'

insights.claim: Even after the outbreak began, Kennedy sent Samoa's prime minister a further four-page letter in November 2019 falsely claiming the MMR vaccine could spur the evolution of more virulent measles strains.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Shows Kennedy doubled down with new misinformation after the fatal outbreak was already underway, rather than retracting his earlier claims, reinforcing the 'pattern, not a slip' characterization.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'Also in November, Kennedy sent the prime minister'

themes.theme: Current political fallout and ongoing relevance

insights.claim: The documents' release comes as the US faces declining vaccination rates and active measles outbreaks that have killed two people this year, including a newborn, with Kennedy responding by spreading misinformation and downplaying the threat as he has in the past.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Ties the historical Samoa episode directly to present-day US public health outcomes, framing Kennedy's pattern of behavior as an ongoing, not historical, risk to vaccination policy.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'The documents land as the US itself is grappling'

insights.claim: Sen. Angela Alsobrooks said Kennedy must resign or be fired immediately, and Hawaii Governor Josh Green, a doctor who personally responded to Samoa's measles outbreak, renewed his own call for Kennedy's resignation.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: A firsthand medical responder to the actual Samoa outbreak publicly renewing calls for removal adds direct-experience credibility to the political pressure building on Kennedy.
